- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/29 (Mon) 00:05
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] A longitudinal study design is a type of research design in which data is collected from the same group of participants over a long period of time.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The purpose of a longitudinal study is to examine changes and patterns of behavior, experiences, or outcomes over time.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Longitudinal studies can be conducted using different research methods, including surveys, interviews, observations, and tests.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Types of longitudinal study designs include: Panel Study Design, Cohort Study Design, Retrospective Study Design, and Prospective Study Design.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In a panel study design, the same group of participants is surveyed at two or more points in time.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In a cohort study design, a group of participants who share a common characteristic is followed over time.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In a retrospective study design, data is collected from participants about past events or experiences.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] In a prospective study design, data is collected from participants over time as events or experiences occur.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Longitudinal studies can provide valuable insights into developmental processes, the impact of interventions, and the relationship between risk factors and outcomes.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of cross-sectional study designs include examining the prevalence of obesity among adults and comparing the prevalence of mental health disorders among different age groups.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Examples of longitudinal study designs include examining the long-term effects of a medication on patients and investigating the development of language skills in children from different socioeconomic backgrounds.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] An example of an observational study design is a researcher studying the eating habits of children in a school cafeteria.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] An example of a non-experimental study design is a researcher studying the relationship between exercise and weight loss through surveys.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Qualitative research focuses on exploring and understanding people's experiences, behaviors, and perceptions through in-depth observation and interviews.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Quantitative research seeks to measure and quantify the frequency, prevalence, or magnitude of a particular phenomenon or relationship using numerical data and statistical analysis.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Qualitative research is characterized by open-ended research questions, small sample sizes, and rich, detailed data.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Quantitative research is characterized by closed-ended research questions, large sample sizes, and standardized data.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Strengths of qualitative research include in-depth exploration and rich data, while limitations
